items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: that's when we had Bechet, Albert Nicholas, Sidney DeParis, and the whole eight -- whole nine of us was on that group

ctx.x: And I mean some of those early the way they were laid out records he did, I mean he (unintelligible), and that was very advanced for its time.

Very (unintelligible). You know, the saddest part about it, you know, the last recording we made practically all the fellows were with him (unintelligible) from New Orleans on that, Wellman Braud Becker Zotty (unintelligible), and it was Sidney Bechet, Albert Nicholas, Zutty Singleton. Then there was (unintelligible). Of course, he was from Indianapolis, him and his brother. They were from Indianapolis, Indiana, and Claude Jones, used to be with Duke. That's the last (unintelligible) requirements.

What happened was that he had -- I think he had a suit against RCA people or either Victor Records, but I think the RCA people were controlling it, and it was somehow or other they'd made a settlement. I think after he got that settlement, that's when he left New York (unintelligible). I was in Atlantic City working with the band.
